![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/925c60dac9f4fde4af85361e064f2eaa3428e22b184d07b7f29026895b7620c4.png)

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-8z$ for $x\ge 0$ and $y\ge 0,$ shown above. 
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}{z}^{2}\,\text{d}V
$$
worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$  represents one-quarter of the sphere of radius $4$ centered at $(0,0,-4).$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=-8z$ in spherical polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =-8z \\ {\rho }^{2} & =-8\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ \\ \rho (\rho +8\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $\rho $ cannot be identical to zero on the entire sphere, we must have $\rho =-8\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/851bf8c7b88641026df202119e7f094632ac477a1a7172baf9ec7c8b986d2ec5.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le -8\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le ϕ\le \pi }.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={z}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)^{2} \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{z}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{-8\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\rho }^{4}{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
